findings.title: 60s eligibility cache returns stale upsampling decisions
findings.body: In src/sentry/api/helpers/error_upsampling.py at line 27-38, is_errors_query_for_error_upsampled_projects caches _are_all_projects_error_upsampled result for 60 seconds keyed by organization.id and hash(tuple(sorted(project_ids))). invalidate_upsampling_cache is never called in the PR, so adding or removing a project from issues.client_error_sampling.project_allowlist has no effect for up to 60s. During the window queries use the wrong aggregation: removed projects keep using sum(sample_weight) and overcount by 1/sample_rate (10x in the added tests), added projects keep using count() and undercount. The key also uses Python hash() so distinct project sets can collide and share an entry, and includes organization.id though the check ignores organization.

findings.title: Upsampling check uses outer dataset instead of scoped_dataset
findings.body: In src/sentry/api/endpoints/organization_events_stats.py at line 221, _get_event_stats receives scoped_dataset which varies for dashboard-widget split (discover vs metrics-enhanced) but passes the outer closure variable dataset to is_errors_query_for_error_upsampled_projects. For example a metrics-enhanced widget split that executes an errors-only query on discover will be judged as a metrics dataset, _should_apply_sample_weight_transform returns False, so no upsampling is applied and sampled errors are undercounted by the sampling factor. The opposite mismatch can enable upsampling for the wrong dataset.

findings.title: Upsampling decision reads original request instead of executed query
findings.body: In src/sentry/api/helpers/error_upsampling.py at line 135, _is_error_focused_query reads request.GET.get("query") while src/sentry/api/endpoints/organization_events_stats.py executes rewritten queries passed as the query argument (e.g. errors_only_query "(orig) AND !event.type:transaction" and transactions_only_query). The eligibility check therefore ignores the actual query: an errors-only split derived from an empty original query will not upsample and will undercount, and a transactions-only split derived from an error query will upsample and overcount or drop rows.

findings.title: Substring error check misclassifies negated and mixed queries
findings.body: In src/sentry/api/helpers/error_upsampling.py at line 137, _is_error_focused_query uses 'event.type:error in query.lower()'. This is True for '!event.type:error' which means NOT error (transactions-only), so a discover transactions-only query will be upsampled with sum(sample_weight) which the code itself says does not exist for transactions, causing wrong counts or missing-column errors. The same check returns True for mixed 'event.type:error OR event.type:transaction' (upsampling transactions) and False for empty queries that include errors, so sampled errors are undercounted.

findings.title: upsampled_count sums nullable weight and truncates
findings.body: In src/sentry/search/events/datasets/discover.py at line 1041, upsampled_count is defined as toInt64(sum(sample_weight)) with no coalesce or rounding. Historical events from before allowlisting, backfilled events, and any mixed transaction rows have NULL/missing sample_weight and will be ignored or make the sum NULL, undercounting. Float weights (e.g. 1/0.3) are truncated by toInt64 instead of rounded, systematically biasing counts low.

findings.title: Internal upsampling aggregate exposed publicly
findings.body: In src/sentry/search/events/datasets/discover.py at line 1041, SnQLFunction("upsampled_count") omits private=True unlike neighboring internal aggregates. Any API user can therefore query upsampled_count() directly via discover, bypassing the allowlist gate in is_errors_query_for_error_upsampled_projects and obtaining raw sum(sample_weight) for non-allowlisted projects, creating unintended API surface and inconsistent counts.

findings.title: Test factory overwrites sample_rate without validation
findings.body: In src/sentry/testutils/factories.py at line 344, _set_sample_rate_from_error_sampling unconditionally overwrites normalized_data["sample_rate"] from contexts.error_sampling.client_sample_rate even if a rate was already set, with no range check. It accepts >1, negative, NaN/inf and non-numeric input (swallowed by bare except: pass), producing unrealistic test events. The integration tests then depend on this path to assert 10x counts, masking ingestion bugs.

findings.title: No coverage for caching entry point
findings.body: In tests/sentry/api/helpers/test_error_upsampling.py at line 19, tests import only _are_all_projects_error_upsampled, _is_error_focused_query, _should_apply_sample_weight_transform and transform_query_columns_for_error_upsampling and never exercise is_errors_query_for_error_upsampled_projects. The 60s cache, hash-based key, and dataset/request interaction that determine real counts are untested. The endpoint tests mock options but never clear the shared cache, allowing stale eligibility to leak across test cases.
